A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Ranked Activation Shift by the same authors. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original RAS benchmark results, activation-editing ablations, layer-selection experiments, corruption tests, and inference-time measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds reference-data sensitivity experiments, AdaSCALE comparisons, and a class-conditional RAS experiment.

M1.justification: The standard RAS procedure is unchanged. Appendix A adds the experimental RAS-CC variant: construct one reference profile per class, predict the label without RAS, then select that class's profile for activation replacement.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same four ID datasets, corresponding near/far OoD datasets, CIFAR-10C, and full-spectrum OoD scenarios. The new experiments vary reference construction within existing coverage; they introduce no new dataset, domain, or task.

E2.justification: v2 Table S9 adds evaluated AdaSCALE-A and AdaSCALE-L comparisons across eight existing settings. Conversely, replacing v1 Table S11 with v2 Table 5 removes ReAct, ASH-P/B/S, DICE, SCALE, and RankFeat from the ID-accuracy comparison. Other benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New Section 5.4 varies the reference-set sample count and compares training data with unlabeled held-out validation data on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet. These are additional experimental settings; the retained benchmark splits, metrics, backbones, and evaluation procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds sensitivity analysis of reference-data quantity and source (Figure 5), plus an ablation testing class-conditioned versus unconditional references (Table S10). Existing layer-selection, excitation/inhibition, activation-profile, corruption, and full-spectrum analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The documented seed counts and existing numerical uncertainty reporting are unchanged. New Figure 5 shows multiple points at individual sample counts, but neither its caption nor Section 5.4 explains their statistical meaning or repetition scheme. Whether this introduces a distinct uncertainty-reporting practice is therefore unclear.

E6.justification: Retained benchmark values match, including all nine detailed benchmark tables and both full-spectrum tables. New Table S9 shows RAS leading FPR in six of eight settings while AdaSCALE variants lead AUROC in seven. Table S10 adds RAS-CC's 84.39 average AUROC versus RAS's 86.55. Figure 5 adds sample-size results; Table 5 adds four architecture-specific accuracy comparisons while removing earlier comparator results.

T1.justification: Equation (6) reverses Gamma from ID-minus-OoD to OoD-minus-ID, aligning its sign with the retained interpretation. Section 2 removes the scoring function's [0,1] restriction. Its revised Equation (1), however, assigns high scores to 0 while the accompanying prose defines 0 as OoD, introducing an internal inconsistency.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows accuracy preservation from 'by construction' to 'empirically.' The conclusion also removes the contrast claiming that other enhancing methods do not guarantee this property. The central hyperparameter-free RAS contribution and activation-shifting claims remain intact.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the reference-data study as showing that retaining the original training set is unnecessary and a small held-out ID sample can suffice. Appendix A adds discussion of AdaSCALE's performance versus its extra backward-pass requirement. Existing variance-compression and activation-profile explanations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The code-access footnote, checkpoint sources, layer-selection details, and timing-test information are retained. v1 Tables S12 and S10 match v2 Tables S14 and S13 in their technical information; no separate new implementation or resource-access specifications accompany the added experiments.

R1.justification: v2 adds the AdaSCALE reference and a focused comparison distinguishing perturbation-induced activation shifts from RAS's reference-profile matching. It explains AdaSCALE's separate treatment through its backward-pass requirement. The remaining cited works and overall research positioning are retained.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main narrative remain unchanged. v2 adds Section 5.4 and two appendix discussions, places Extended Results before Covariate Shift, removes the standalone appendix ID Accuracy section, and makes limited terminology, caption, and keyword edits.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 5 and Tables S9–S10, and replaces the appendix accuracy table with a compact main-text table covering more architectures but fewer methods. Figure 1 gains a dataset legend. Other figures and tables are largely retained with relocation, renumbering, caption formatting, and layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: The reference-data study, class-conditional ablation, and AdaSCALE comparison strengthen practical and comparative evidence. Replacing the accuracy guarantee with an empirical claim and correcting Equation (6) improve precision. These constitute a limited net gain, tempered by removal of comparator accuracy results and the new label inconsistency in Equation (1); the main benchmark evidence is unchanged.
